title: Ext maps intertwine a natural isomorphism of composite exact functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal C_3,\mathcal C_4$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with Ext groups in chosen universes [def-pc-ext]. Let $G:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $J:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_3$, $J':\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_4$, and $G_W:\mathcal C_3\to\mathcal C_4$ be additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Let $c:J'G\xrightarrow{\sim}G_WJ$ be a natural isomorphism. For $A,F\in\mathcal C_1$, $n\geq0$, and $x\in\operatorname{Ext}^n(A,F)$, write $G(x)$ for the map on Ext induced by the exact functor $G$. Then
$$J'(G(x))\cdot[c_F]=[c_A]\cdot G_W(J(x))\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Ext}^n(J'GA,G_WJF),$$
where brackets denote degree-zero Ext classes and the left expression is postcomposition, while the right expression is precomposition. No adjunction, geometry, scalar representations, or bijectivity is assumed.

source.place: Functoriality of cohomology (01F7) and derived functors of exact functors (015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); specialization to derived morphisms between single complexes.

proof.text: Prove a private exact-functor composition comparison with independent Ext universes. Use mapDerivedCategoryNatIso followed by mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and the proved shift-compatibility instances in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Shift.ExactFunctor. Normalize the three single-complex comparison components directly using the Mathlib definitions mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor and singleFunctorIsoCompQ, with localized conv simplification; no separate singleComparison_hom theorem is declared. The factorization identities reduce the endpoint comparison to complex morphisms, verified degreewise at zero and away from zero.

Apply Ext hom injectivity and expand Ext.comp_hom, Ext.mk₀_hom and Ext.mapExactFunctor_hom. Obtain the inverse endpoint comparison by cancellation. Apply ShiftedHom.map_naturality to the derived morphism representing x, conjugate by the endpoint single-complex comparisons, and simplify the shift comparison for composite functors. This proves the private composition comparison without identifying the universes used to shrink Ext in the three categories.

Apply the private composition comparison first to G, J', H = G ⋙ J' and the identity isomorphism. Simplifying the degree-zero identity classes gives x.mapExactFunctor (G ⋙ J') = (x.mapExactFunctor G).mapExactFunctor J'. Apply it a second time to J, GW, H = G ⋙ J' and c, then substitute the first equality. This is exactly the claimed square, with the original four independent Ext universes and unchanged hypotheses.

lean.statement:
theorem mapExactFunctor_square
    {C₁ : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C₁] [Abelian C₁] [HasExt.{w₁} C₁]
    {C₂ : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C₂] [Abelian C₂] [HasExt.{w₂} C₂]
    {C₃ : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} C₃] [Abelian C₃] [HasExt.{w₃} C₃]
    {C₄ : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} C₄] [Abelian C₄] [HasExt.{w₄} C₄]
    (G : C₁ ⥤ C₂) [G.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G]
    (J : C₁ ⥤ C₃) [J.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits J] [PreservesFiniteColimits J]
    (J' : C₂ ⥤ C₄) [J'.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits J'] [PreservesFiniteColimits J']
    (GW : C₃ ⥤ C₄) [GW.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits GW] [PreservesFiniteColimits GW]
    (c : G ⋙ J' ≅ J ⋙ GW) {A F : C₁} (n : ℕ) (x : Ext A F n) :
    ((x.mapExactFunctor G).mapExactFunctor J').comp (Ext.mk₀ (c.app F).hom)
        (add_zero n) =
      (Ext.mk₀ (c.app A).hom).comp ((x.mapExactFunctor J).mapExactFunctor GW)
        (zero_add n)
